proof.surface: The real AskGate handler on the bash path under pi-envoy's suite, with the fake Dispatch serving the stored brief.md holding #window (no live session can make the charter revise an upload on purpose).

proof.negativeControl: On HEAD's askgate-core.ts it fails: the result is `<advisor-gate advisor="AskGate" outcome="breaker">Third attempt after two refusals of this call on its target…`, the reviewer's reproduction.

proof.criterion: An upload whose rules check judged only part of its asks counts its charter refusals on the judged ask, so the warned third resend trips.
proof.surface: The same, with no Dispatch so the stored-version read fails (ruleAsksPartial true).
proof.observed: 'an upload whose rules check judged only part of its asks counts its charter refusals on the judged ask, so sent unchanged a third time it goes out on the breaker as warned': warning on refusal 2 only, the third send outcome="breaker".

filesChanged: packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/askgate-core.ts — callKeys replaces breakerThings: one key set per call (an upload's asks plus its own upload key from its trimmed name and a sha256 of its content, never WHOLE_CALL); tripped() matches it and refusalThings counts a subset of it, filtered against it in one place; doc comments corrected.
packages/pi-envoy/extensions/askgate/askgate.test.ts — the three tests above and a helper; every earlier test unchanged.
trickyParts: tripped() runs before the rules check, so the key set cannot depend on the rules result; refusalThings picks the subset after it, so a refusal's keys are always keys the same call sent again yields.
